concept.name: Commodity channel index
concept.definition: Donald Lambert's oscillator (Commodities magazine, 1980) measuring how far the typical price has deviated from its moving average, expressed in units of mean absolute deviation scaled by 0.015 so that roughly 70-80% of readings fall between -100 and +100.
concept.intuition: CCI normalizes 'how stretched is price from its own average?' - excursions beyond +/-100 mark statistically unusual strength or weakness that can flag a new trend or an extreme.
concept.mechanics: Compute the typical price TP = (H+L+C)/3, subtract its n-period SMA (default 20), and divide by 0.015 times the mean absolute deviation of TP from that SMA. Used for +/-100 trend-emergence signals, +/-200 extremes, and confirmed divergences.
concept.formula: CCI = (TP - SMA(TP, n)) / (0.015 x MeanDev), TP = (High + Low + Close)/3, MeanDev = (1/n) x sum of |TP_i - SMA(TP, n)| over the last n periods.
concept.failure_modes: CCI is unbounded, so overbought/oversold levels are arbitrary and must be calibrated per security; zero-line crosses whipsaw, and in strong trends CCI stays beyond +/-100 while price keeps running.
concept.misconceptions: Despite the name it is not commodity-specific, and +/-100 is a statistical convention, not a hard ceiling - the oscillator routinely exceeds it.
concept.example: TP = 24, 20-period SMA of TP = 22, mean deviation 1.33: CCI = (24-22)/(0.015 x 1.33) ~ +100.
